scalesUsed.notes: G - A - Bb - C - D - E - F - G
scalesUsed.application: Underpins the main riff and verse progressions; the natural 6th degree (E) gives the riff its distinctive funk-rock drive without the somber weight of natural minor
Foundation for Mark Knopfler's aggressive double-stop fills and signature blues bends

scalesUsed.notes: G - Bb - C - Db - D - F
scalesUsed.application: The flatted 5th (Db) provides gritty chromatic tension during transitions and fill licks

keyAndScale.keySignature: Two flats (Bb, Eb) in G natural minor, but the prominent natural E note consistently shifts the tonal color to G Dorian
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: G minor is the relative minor of Bb major; G Dorian borrows its pitch collection from F major

mainProgression.description: A high-octane rock progression anchored around G minor. Knopfler voices the chords using two-note double stops on the D and G strings rather than full barre chords, leaving maximum room for percussion and bass.

sectionProgressions.progression: Gm - F - Gm - Bb - C - Gm
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: i - bVII - i - bIII - IV - i
sectionProgressions.description: Syncopated fingerstyle rock riff bouncing between low G pedal notes and snappy fourth-interval double stops
Descending minor progression driven by tight palm muting and ghost note pops
Ascending major lift building dynamic harmonic pressure before resolving to the chorus hook
Powerhouse stadium cadence featuring punchy downbeat accents and soaring vocal unison

harmonicFunction: Gm (i) - Tonic minor chord anchoring the dark, driving tonal center
F (bVII) - Subtonic chord providing classic rock momentum and avoiding classical leading-tone stiffness
Eb (bVI) - Submediant chord adding poignant harmonic weight in the verse and chorus turnarounds
D (V) - Dominant major chord delivering strong tension that pulls naturally back to Gm
C (IV) - Major IV chord highlighting the Dorian natural 6th (E) in the pre-chorus climb

techniques.name: Bare-Finger Claw-Hammer Picking
techniques.description: Mark Knopfler's signature fingerstyle attack using the thumb on bass strings while snapping double stops with the index and middle fingers, producing an aggressive percussive bite impossible with a flatpick

notes: Rest the fleshy heel of your pick hand against the bridge saddles for selective palm muting
Use the thumb exclusively for root notes on strings 6 and 5
Snap the index and middle fingers upward under strings 4 and 3 to create the snappy double-stop pop
Incorporate ghost notes by slapping strings against fretwires with relaxed fret-hand fingers
Keep the wrist supple to maintain the syncopated 134 BPM boogie pulse
sequence: Strike the low G root on fret 3 with the thumb
Pluck the double stop at fret 5 (strings 4 and 3) simultaneously with index and middle fingers
Release fret-hand pressure immediately for a staccato percussive snap
Execute the quick hammer-on slide from fret 3 to fret 5 with fingers 1 and 3
tips: Do not use a flatpick; skin-on-string contact is essential for the round bottom and biting pop
Practice the thumb-to-fingers coordination slowly at 90 BPM before pushing to full tempo
Focus on silencing unplayed strings with your fret-hand index finger pad
details.progression: Gm - F - Gm - Bb - C - Gm

techniques.name: Cocked-Wah Mid-Range Phrasing
techniques.description: Utilizing a wah-wah pedal parked stationary at roughly 60% of its travel to create a sharp resonant peak in the mid frequencies, giving notes singing vocal presence and immediate cut

notes: Engage a standard wah pedal and sweep forward until you hear the nasal, vocal sweet spot
Leave the pedal rocker stationary throughout the phrase
Combine with bridge humbucker and moderate tube overdrive to generate singing harmonics
Control note sustain by applying wide, relaxed horizontal wrist vibrato
sequence: Set your overdrive amp to moderate crunch
Rock the wah to find the 800Hz-1.2kHz resonant boost
Pick firmly over the bridge pickup to excite rich upper-harmonic overtones
Let sustained notes feed back subtly into the amplifier
tips: If you do not own a wah pedal, use an EQ pedal with a steep +6dB bell boost centered at 1 kHz
A humbucker-equipped guitar (Les Paul or Strat with bridge humbucker) yields the thickest tone
Keep your guitar volume rolled back slightly to 8 for rhythm, then dial to 10 for lead fills

sections.name: Intro Ambient Build & Monster Riff Entrance
sections.description: Atmospheric synth pad and Sting's haunting 'I want my MTV' falsetto culminate in a thunderous drum roll, launching into the most famous fingerstyle rock riff in history.
sections.progression: Gm - F - Gm - Bb - C - Gm
notes: Thumb snaps low G root while fingers pop the upper fourths on D and G strings
Keep the rhythm strictly syncopated on sixteenth-note upbeats
Mute immediately after each chord pop for crisp percussive definition
Let the cocked-wah midrange cut through the drum groove

sections.name: Verse 1 Fingerstyle Comping & Ghost Pops
sections.description: Rhythm drops into a sparse, percussive groove under the narrative vocals. Knopfler peppers the space with muted string slaps and subtle double-stop stabs.
notes: Keep chord stabs short and snappy on the backbeat
Use fret-hand dampening to stop string resonance instantly
Listen to the snare and kick to lock into the pocket
Leave space for the storytelling vocal delivery

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Modulated Lift
sections.description: Harmonic tension builds rapidly as the progression steps up through Bb, C, and D, expanding the sonic canvas ahead of the explosive chorus.
notes: Open up the dynamic envelope from quiet comping to ringing drive
Accent the syncopated chord transitions on the upbeats
Allow the major thirds to ring out clearly to signal the tonal lift
Drive through the D major chord to set up the Gm return

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Groove
sections.description: The full band locks into a heavy stadium rock cadence with punchy Gm, Eb, and F chords supporting the iconic vocal anthem.
notes: Deliver bold, resolute downstrokes on chord changes
Emphasize the low Eb bass note for harmonic weight
Blend fingerstyle attack with authoritative wrist snap
Lock directly into the cymbal crashes and snare accents

sections.name: Knopfler Signature Fill Solo
sections.description: Knopfler unleashes a blistering array of fingerpicked blues-rock phrases, blending whole-step bends on the B string with ringing fourth-interval double stops.
sections.progression: Gm - F - Gm - Bb - C - Gm
notes: Execute the signature 8th fret whole-step bend on string 2 up to D
Pluck descending pentatonic runs with index and middle finger alternate picking
Add biting vibrato using the weight of the forearm rather than thumb squeeze
Emphasize the Dorian natural 6th (E on 9th fret G string)

sections.name: Outro Extended Jam & Fadeout Licks
sections.description: A celebrated 4-minute masterclass in rhythmic variation. Knopfler continuously reinterprets the main riff with syncopated blues ornaments as the track fades.
notes: Vary the attack from whispered thumb pulses to snapping double stops
Incorporate microtonal blues curls on the minor 3rd (Bb)
Maintain seamless tempo consistency across extended playing
Keep the groove relaxed yet rhythmically razor sharp

guitar.recommended: Gibson 1980 Les Paul Standard (58 Reissue) or Schecter Custom Strat with humbuckers
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker (PAF style) with volume rolled back slightly to 8.5 for touch-sensitive dynamics

amp.recommended: Laney 100W Supergroup / Marshall JCM800 combo into 4x12 Celestion cabinet
alternatives: Fender Blues Deluxe with overdrive pedal

effects.distortion: Amp overdrive supplemented by smooth preamp drive
effects.reverb: Subtle plate reverb with 1.5s decay to simulate studio room ambiance
effects.other: Dunlop CryBaby or Morley Wah left stationary in middle position (cocked wah)

beginner.title: Mastering the Core Riff Shapes
steps: Learn the two-note fourth voicings at fret 5 and fret 3 on the D and G strings
Practice alternating between the thumb on low G (fret 3) and the upper chord stabs
Work with a metronome at 80 BPM until the chord transitions feel seamless
beginner.goals: Play the foundational 2-bar riff cleanly with steady timing

intermediate.title: Fingerstyle Snap & Palm Muting
steps: Adopt bare-finger claw-hammer technique without using a flatpick
Master the fleshy palm mute on the bridge saddle to control string ringing
Incorporate ghost slaps and upbeat accents at full 134 BPM tempo
intermediate.goals: Execute the complete verse and chorus rhythm tracks with authentic feel

advanced.title: Cocked-Wah Phrasing & Lead Fills
steps: Dial in cocked-wah resonant frequencies and bridge humbucker response
Transcribe and perform Knopfler's expressive whole-step bends and double-stop fills
Improvise over the G Dorian vamp using natural 6th targeting and vocal vibrato
advanced.goals: Perform the entire 8-minute album track with professional phrasing and dynamics

sameArtist.title: Sultans of Swing
sameArtist.similarity: Showcases Mark Knopfler's clean fingerstyle picking, triad embellishments, and fast arpeggios

sameArtist.title: Brothers in Arms
sameArtist.similarity: Legendary Les Paul singing sustain, volume swells, and emotional Dorian/Aeolian phrasing

commonMistakes: Using a flatpick instead of bare fingers, which robs the riff of its snappy percussive bite
Letting unplayed strings ring out rather than dampening with the palm and fret-hand fingers
Rushing the syncopated upbeats instead of laying back into the pocket at 134 BPM
Setting the wah pedal too high, resulting in harsh, piercing treble rather than warm vocal mids
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Thumb and finger independence drill on strings 6, 4, and 3
10 mins: Slow metronome practice of the main 2-bar riff at 90, 110, and 134 BPM
10 mins: Verse palm-muting and ghost-pop timing work against a drum loop
10 mins: Lead fill practice focusing on whole-step pitch accuracy and wide wrist vibrato
focusAreas: Pick-hand fingerstyle ergonomics and thumb-finger separation
Precise staccato muting on fourth-interval double stops
Dynamic contrast between whispering verses and thunderous choruses
metronomeWork: Start practicing the signature intro riff at 80 BPM to lock in thumb-finger coordination
Increase by 6 BPM increments once 4 consecutive clean repetitions are achieved
Set the metronome clicks strictly to beats 2 and 4 to develop authentic rock backbeat groove
